{"id": "22:11/q19", "question": "What theological lesson is drawn from conditional worship and trials?", "turns_on": "Whether the moral focus is steadfastness, inward intention, God's justice, or associating other powers with Him.", "positions": [{"id": "22:11/q19/p1", "position": "Steadfast worship means gratitude and patience, while conditional service exposes self-interest and loss.", "reasons": "Al-Thaʿlabī says gratitude and patience would cure instability. Sahl al-Tustarī portrays the believer as charging ahead through monotheism, prophetic emulation and supplication; a reported saying from Zayd ibn Aslam says obedience admits one to Paradise and disobedience is refusal. Iṣlāḥī says God alone controls benefit and harm, and trials met with submission increase faith and reward."}, {"id": "22:11/q19/p2", "position": "Appetite or confidence in one's own deeds can masquerade as worship.", "reasons": "Tustarī says immediate pleasure makes a person content and deprivation drives him toward disbelief. {"id": "22:12/q01", "question": "Who is the person invoking besides God?", "turns_on": "Whether the surrounding apostasy describes the caller specifically, and whether invocation of idols excludes a Jewish referent.", "positions": [{"id": "22:12/q01/p1", "position": "A worshipper who turns back to unbelief after a trial and then invokes idols.", "reasons": "Al-Tabari connects this with the precarious worshipper's trial and apostasy in 22:11; Ibn Zayd calls it disbelief after belief. {"id": "22:12/q04", "question": "What does invoking something besides God imply?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "22:12/q04/p1", "position": "It wrongly transfers worship, trust or control over harm and benefit away from God.", "reasons": "Al-Biqa'i says all besides God are beneath the possessor of every perfection; worship is owed through chosen action rather than compelled natural behavior. {"id": "26:181/q01", "question": "What does the command to fulfill the measure require?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "26:181/q01/p1", "position": "Give the full amount due, without shortfall, when measuring goods.", "reasons": "Muqātil, Yaḥyā b. {"id": "26:181/q02", "question": "Who are the loss-makers, and what does the word mean?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "26:181/q02/p1", "position": "They cause others loss by reducing their measure, weight, or due rights.", "reasons": "Yaḥyā b. Al-Wāḥidī reports the commentators' identification of those who reduce measure or weight, and Abū ʿUbayd's equivalence of khasartu and akhsartu the scale as making it deficient; he compares the short-measurers of 83:3 and says yukhsirūn is linguistically permissible.
